tool_args.rationale: The five short-horizon rows leave the slow-timescale adaptation parameter—and therefore the long-horizon forecast—poorly identified. The slow-horizon probe is the targeted, lowest-cost available measurement for resolving that ambiguity.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the 5-parameter sink-coupled dual-horizon adaptation model from the five initial rows
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The short-H observations do not identify the slow adaptation timescale needed for the H=23.2 forecast.
A fine trajectory is less directly informative about the long-horizon reversal than the slow-horizon discriminating probe.
It is irrelevant to the identified ambiguity and would add cost without resolving it.

considered_alternatives.option: Dual-horizon endogenous adaptation without sink coupling
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The sink-gradient signature supports a coupled sink effect; the current rows do not distinguish its contribution robustly.
